Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G3340; unrepentant:--impenitent.
BiblicalUsage: Once, in the sentence on the hard heart: after thy hardness and impenitent heart treasurest up unto thyself wrath against the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God. The word is unrepentant, the heart that will not turn, and the wrath is treasured up like money in a storehouse, day by day.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for impenitent carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the picture, that a heart that will not turn is storing up wrath the way a miser stores gold.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
